subject: [PATCH v5 04/11] mm: zswap: add range lookup for large-folio swapin

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary:
Author acknowledged that the folio is locked and the result will be stable, proposed a patch to reject mixed zswap/disk backing before starting the read in swap_cache_alloc() function.

Author acknowledged a potential issue with writeback interfering with zswap, decided to stick with the original implementation.

2026-07-24.patch_summary: This patch adds a range lookup feature to the zswap compression algorithm, allowing it to handle large folios by scanning the covered range and checking if any slots are still in zswap. If no slot is found, it returns -ENOENT so the caller can read from the backing device. If any slot is present, it fails the large-folio read to prevent returning partially initialized data. The patch also introduces a new function `zswap_is_present` to enable PMD swap-entry consumers to make range decisions before attempting PMD-order swapin.

reviews.author: Nhat Pham
reviews.summary: Reviewer Nhat Pham suggested moving zswap_is_present() call to __swap_cache_add_check() to allow backoff before folio allocation
reviews.raw_body:
If you move it to __swap_cache_add_check(), you can potentially
backoff even before the folio allocation? :)

reviews.author: Usama Arif (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the zswap writeback and swap-cache insertion need to be serialized, agreed to add a check in __swap_cache_add_check() to reject mixed zswap/disk backing before allocating a large folio.
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks Nhat! Yes, this looks much much better as well:

@@ -190,6 +191,15 @@ static int __swap_cache_add_check(struct swap_cluster_info *ci,
        if (nr == 1)
                return 0;
 
+       /*
+        * The cluster lock serializes swap-cache insertion with zswap
+        * writeback. Reject mixed zswap/disk backing before allocating a
+        * large folio and recheck it before adding the folio to swap cache.
+        */
+       if (zswap_is_present(swp_entry(swp_type(targ_entry),
+                                      round_down(swp_offset(targ_entry), nr)), nr))
+               return -EBUSY;
